resources.string: How long to wait for a TCP connection to a daemon to open.
How long to wait for the response to one request on an open connection.

How long to wait for the response to a session stop or remove. A removal ends the session\'s processes and deletes its worktree checkout, which takes longer than a list request; the dialog reports a timeout as an unknown outcome.

How long to wait for the response to a new session. The daemon starts the agent before it answers, which takes far longer than a list request. A timeout is reported as an unknown outcome and the request is never repeated.
How many times a failed attach is tried, the first try included. Applies to the next terminal you open.
How long to wait between two attach tries. Applies to the next terminal you open.
How often the session list is read again from each daemon to correct what the event stream missed.
How often each connected host is asked for the daemons on its overlay (host discovery); it is also asked when it connects.
How long one host discovery exchange may take once connected. The daemon probes its peers before it answers, which takes longer than a list request.
How long to wait before the first reconnect to a daemon; the wait doubles per consecutive failure. It may not exceed the longest wait.
The longest wait between two reconnects, and how long a connection must hold before the failure count resets. It may not be below the first wait.
How often a health probe detects a silently dead connection to a daemon. A dead connection is noticed within this plus the probe timeout.
How long one health probe, connecting included, may take before the connection is declared dead and re-established.
How often an attached terminal checks that its connection is alive. Applies to the next terminal you open.
How long a liveness check of an attached terminal may take before the attach fails. Applies to the next terminal you open.
How long to wait before an open terminal whose attachment broke attaches again; the wait doubles per consecutive failure. It may not exceed the longest wait. Applies to the next terminal you open.
The longest wait between two re-attaches, and how long an attach must hold before the failure count resets. It may not be below the first wait. Applies to the next terminal you open.

How long an open terminal may stay without an attachment before it stops retrying and shows a final error. A session the daemon reports ended or removed stops it at once. Applies to the next terminal you open.
How long a session must stay idle, with no running subagent or background task, before it is shown as Idle instead of Working.
The longest badge text (Work link or role) a session row shows before it is cut with an ellipsis.
The longest section title (project label or Work item) the By project and By Work item views show before it is cut with an ellipsis.
The longest value the session details screen shows before its middle is replaced by an ellipsis. Copying always takes the full value.

How many records are requested per page when the attention notifications are read. The page is halved while the daemon reports it as too large, and a page of one that is still too large fails the read.
The terminal width in columns that a new session starts with; the terminal view resizes it when you open the session.
The terminal height in rows that a new session starts with; the terminal view resizes it when you open the session.
How long a new session started from a group waits for the daemon to list it before it stays in Inbox instead.
The size limit of one log file. The log keeps the active file and one rotated file, so it never takes more than twice this.
